summary: Iteration 15: Validated Supabase Auth migration. Backend pytest: 13/13 PASS (login customer+admin, /api/auth/me, /api/bills, /api/auth/register, forgot-password known+unknown email, admin/stats, /v2/subscription/current, /v2/predict-bills). Frontend E2E: forgot-password-link visible on /login -> /forgot-password loads with email input + Send Reset Link btn -> submit shows 'Check your email' confirmation with reset-sent-message testid; customer login -> /dashboard renders fully (Total Bills 7, Outstanding $1010.95, Wallet $500, AI Bill Intelligence insight, upcoming bills); Bill Intelligence page accessible; admin login auto-redirects to /admin and Financial Overview shows data. CRITICAL FINDING: Supabase Auth is wired but ALL real auth flows fall back to custom JWT — seeded users (test@/admin@billseasypay.com) are NOT in Supabase Auth ('Invalid login credentials'), AND Supabase admin.create_user returns 'User not allowed' for new registrations (so register also falls back to custom JWT). Net behavior: works end-to-end via fallback, but the migration goal is not achieved. Also FORGOT-PASSWORD endpoint silently swallows Supabase failure ('User with this email not found') and still returns generic 200 — no real email will be sent for seeded users since they don't exist in Supabase Auth. Additional REGRESSION suspected: /dashboard/annual-plan main content area renders EMPTY for Standard user (iter14 had it showing full forecast). Backend /api/v2/predict-bills returns 200, so this looks like a frontend-only regression.

minor.issue: Silently returns 200 even when sb.auth.admin.generate_link fails ('User with this email not found'). For all currently-seeded users, password recovery will NOT actually send any email since they don't exist in Supabase Auth. Endpoint behaves correctly for unknown emails (intentional non-leak), but for valid app users that are NOT in Supabase Auth this gives the user a false sense that an email was sent.

Supabase create_user returns 'User not allowed' (likely Auth signups disabled in Supabase project settings OR rate-limited) — code silently falls back to custom JWT. supabase_uid never gets linked. Result: user is created in app DB only, defeating the Supabase Auth migration.

Supabase sign_in_with_password returns 'Invalid login credentials' for test@billseasypay.com and admin@billseasypay.com because seeded users were never created in Supabase Auth. Falls back to bcrypt verification — works, but migration is no-op for existing users. Need a one-time backfill: for each app user, call sb.auth.admin.create_user with their current password (or trigger password-reset emails).

References undefined name SUPABASE_JWT_SECRET (lines 64,68,77,81). If any real Supabase JWT ever reaches decode_token() (called by get_admin_user at server.py:1171), this will raise NameError -> 500. Currently masked because no Supabase tokens are ever issued (see register/login items above). Fix: SUPABASE_JWT_SECRET = os.environ.get('SUPABASE_JWT_SECRET','') at module load.

Uses sb.auth.admin.get_user(token) — this method does NOT exist on SyncGoTrueAdminAPI in the installed supabase-py version (AttributeError raised, then silently caught and 401 returned). Verified via direct SDK call. Use sb.auth.get_user(token) (no .admin) instead, or decode the Supabase JWT with SUPABASE_JWT_SECRET.

ui_bugs.issue: Main content area renders EMPTY for Standard tier user test@billseasypay.com. Sidebar/header render but no forecast cards, chart, or upgrade message — page body keywords (Forecast, smoothed, Peak, Variance, Upgrade) all absent after 5s wait. /api/v2/predict-bills returns 200 in backend, so this is a frontend-only regression vs iter14.

integration_issues.flow: Forgot password for existing seeded user
integration_issues.issue: UI shows 'Check your email' success but no recovery email will ever land — seeded users are not in Supabase Auth (see backend issue above). End user will be stuck thinking reset link is coming.

action_items: FIX (HIGH): /dashboard/annual-plan renders empty for Standard user — verify ForecastDashboard component is mounted, check console for React errors, and confirm /api/v2/predict-bills response shape matches what UI expects. Regression vs iter14.

FIX (HIGH): Backfill existing app users into Supabase Auth — currently seeded admin & customer cannot use Supabase password-recovery because they don't exist in Supabase. Either create them in Supabase Auth via admin.create_user with current passwords, or generate password-reset links and force first-time setup.

FIX (HIGH): Investigate 'User not allowed' on sb.auth.admin.create_user during /api/auth/register — likely Supabase project setting (Auth -> Providers -> Email: enable signups, or service-role permissions). Without this, NEW users never get Supabase identity.
FIX: utils/auth.py uses undefined SUPABASE_JWT_SECRET (will NameError if a Supabase token ever reaches decode_token). Add: SUPABASE_JWT_SECRET = os.environ.get('SUPABASE_JWT_SECRET','').

FIX: utils/auth.get_current_user calls sb.auth.admin.get_user(token) which does NOT exist in installed supabase SDK (AttributeError, silently caught). Use sb.auth.get_user(token) or verify JWT locally with SUPABASE_JWT_SECRET.
Consider surfacing Supabase failures (do not silently 200 forgot-password / silently fallback on register) at least in backend logs with WARN/ERROR level for observability.
critical_code_review_comments: Carry-over from iter14: server.py still 2959 lines, route handlers should be split (routes/auth.py etc).
utils/auth.py: passlib bcrypt warning persists — pin bcrypt<4.
utils/auth.py: decode_token() references SUPABASE_JWT_SECRET that is never defined — latent NameError.
utils/auth.py: get_current_user uses non-existent sb.auth.admin.get_user — Supabase token verification path is effectively dead code.

server.py /auth/register: catching the entire Supabase exception block silently masks 'User not allowed' — log.warning is good, but the migration is failing in prod-equivalent without anyone noticing.

server.py /auth/forgot-password: returning generic 200 message is correct for security, but the inner try/except should at least DETECT 'User not in Supabase Auth' and trigger a different recovery path (e.g., custom email with token) so legitimate users aren't silently blocked.

rca of the issue.supabase_no_op: Supabase create/sign_in/get_user calls all fail (User not allowed / Invalid credentials / AttributeError) because (a) project Auth settings likely disallow service-role signups OR users were never backfilled, and (b) SDK version's auth-admin does not expose get_user.
